children: The Federal Reserve will need to adapt how it implements monetary policy as financial market structures evolve, New York Fed President John Williams said Tuesday.

“As markets evolve, we must ensure that policy tools are fit for purpose to carry out their necessary functions,” Williams said in prepared remarks at the 2026 U.S. Treasury Market Conference in New York.

Williams pointed to the expansion of central clearing as a key example of how market structure is changing. He said the industry had already begun expanding infrastructure for cleared repo and cash trading, with activity shifting from uncleared to cleared markets “ahead of schedule.”

The shift is important for the Fed because changes in market structure can affect how effectively its policy tools control interest rates and support financial-market functioning. Williams said the Fed's ample-reserves framework, adopted in 2019, relies on administered rates alongside overnight reverse repo and standing repo operations.
Williams said the move toward central clearing would require the New York Fed to continue studying how changes in Treasury and repo market structure impact its operations.

He pointed to the earlier transition from bilateral repo to tri-party repo as an example, saying the New York Fed's Open Market Trading Desk had moved its operations into the markets where trades occurred as the structure changed.
“The evolution of financial market structure leads to the evolution of how we carry out monetary policy effectively,” Williams said.

He identified three principles for effective monetary-policy implementation: interest-rate control, low opportunity costs for holding reserves, and elasticity, meaning the supply of reserves can adjust as underlying demand changes.
Williams also said stablecoins and tokenized finance would be an important focus at the conference, calling tokenized finance a topic that could shape financial markets in coming years.
Williams said the New York Fed would remain focused on understanding changes in market structure and their implications for monetary-policy transmission.
“It is imperative that as the markets evolve, we have the policy tools that are right for that purpose and are well designed to function effectively under all circumstances,” Williams said.

title: Policy tools must adapt as market structure shifts, Williams says
